content_text: Have you ever wondered at what age babies start talking? Without a doubt, it is a great question that many times fills parents with uncertainty. Undoubtedly, there are several factors that allow a child to adequately develop their language and, as they grow, improve it. Now, if you want to know when do babies start talking, keep reading this article. When do babies start talking? Your baby will likely develop different ways to communicate with you. From the way babies cry or their facial expressions and body movements to starting to use sounds and words. As your baby approaches their first birthday, they may already be communicating with you by pointing at things or by crawling toward objects they want to reach. Perhaps they also imitate gestures that they see other people make when they speak. Download our free app and start tracking your baby’s development! Also, it is very likely that your child is already babbling and making noises or sounds that will later transform into syllables. At this age, your baby might say “mom” by accident. It will be very exciting, but, at this point, they will repeat the same word all day as an indicator that they’re practicing it. You will be able to notice this process when your baby is between 8 and 12 months old. Although your little one won’t use the words in the same way as adults, they will begin to practice them. It is very likely that they understand most of the things you say to them. Since you have spoken to them since they were born, your baby has developed a lot their language comprehension; more than you imagine! Helping them with their language development There are many ways to help your baby reinforce their linguistic skills. They are practiced naturally from 3 months on, at which point some children tend to start babbling. One of the main ways to help your little one is through your interactions, since, according to Unicef, emotional development is essential in the early stages of a baby. Language skills are not alien to this. Interacting and playing with your child will help them regulate their emotions and organize their cognitive processes. In fact, physical contact, experimenting with facial expressions, and exploring their body are fundamental elements for the adequate development of a baby’s capacity for symbolization and empathy. Another excellent way to foster language is through picture books. These promote language development and can be incorporated into a baby’s life from an early age. This will help them have a much more developed abstraction process. When you read to your child, if they’re already in the talking stage, let them participate, speak, and answer questions about what they are seeing or hearing about the story.
